minutes.headline: Sewer Commission backed buying the Munilink billing software and approved a connection fee and year-end encumbrances.
minutes.summary: The commission heard a staff presentation on replacing its three-system billing process with Munilink and voted to support the project, pending talks with town management, the accountant and the treasurer. It also approved a privilege fee for a new connection, FY22 year-end encumbrances and a final commitment. The sewer superintendent reviewed maintenance plans, and staff reported on an extension survey, grease trap permits and invoices.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted to strongly support replacing its three-system billing process with Munilink, pending talks with town management, the accountant and the treasurer.
The commission assessed a privilege fee for connecting 17 Highland Street to the sewer main; the vote outcome was not audible.
The commission accepted the FY22 year-end encumbrances, including debt service, generator maintenance and the Wright-Pierce SSO project.
The commission accepted the final commitment for end-of-year final reads, after staff said the enterprise ended FY22 slightly ahead of its estimated loss.
Staff will check with the town manager whether any ARPA money remains available for sewer needs.

why_it_matters: Sewer billing software is a recurring cost paid from sewer rates, and the commission signaled support before funding is settled; staff suggested FY23 money, possibly spread over two fiscal years.
Whether ARPA money can cover any of this, and whether the town manager, accountant and treasurer agree to integrate Munilink, will decide who pays and when.
watch_next: Next meeting on July 26, to be held by Zoom or hybrid, when prior minutes return for approval with a correction.
Staff answers from the town manager, accountant and treasurer on Munilink integration and ARPA availability.
